column1: # Refusal sites that scripts/ratchet.sh does not require an assertion for, and
# the reason for each. Three columns: the site id from docs/review/refusal-sites.tsv,
# the disposition, and the reason. Only "unreachable" is accepted; every other
# site has to be behaviourally covered.
# Every one of these was checked rather than argued. The check applies that one
# mutation to a clone of the base database, calls the function on an input that
# reaches the guard, and compares the answer with the unmutated answer. All
# eleven give the same answer, which is what "unreachable" means here: the guard
# is reached, it is removed, and no caller can tell.
# That is not the same as dead code and it is not a path nobody found. It is a
# function with more than one way to say the same thing. Worth knowing, because
# a reader of the source would count eleven refusals that are not there.
# The first version of this check reported the two generate_inferred_history
# rows as equivalent because both the mutated and the unmutated call returned
# the same error, which came from a fixture that had never been created. Two
# runs agreeing is not evidence when they agree on having failed.
# id
resolve_subject_name:notfound:1
column3: The fall-through gives the same answer. With the guard removed the resolver row is all nulls, quote_ident(null) is null, to_regclass(null) is null, and the next guard returns the same null.

column1: resolve_subject_name:earlyreturn:1
column3: Same as the guard above it: this is the return that guard performs, and the path it would have skipped returns null as well.

column1: resolve_subject_name:guard:1
column3: Removing it lets execute run against a relation that does not exist, which raises, which the function's own exception handler turns into the same null.

column1: resolve_subject_name:earlyreturn:2
column3: Same as the guard above it.

column1: resolve_subject_name:earlyreturn:3
column3: This is the return inside the exception handler. Removing it falls through to the final return of a variable that was never assigned, which is null.

column1: node_bin_shares:notfound:1
column3: A lot that does not exist has no lineage, so the recursive term finds no bins and the function returns the empty set either way.

column1: node_bin_shares:permissive:1
column3: may_see_all_of coalesces to false inside itself and can never return null, so the outer default is never the value that is used. Changing false to true there changes nothing.

column1: node_history:notfound:1
column3: A lot that does not exist has no events, so the query returns the empty set either way.

column1: node_history:permissive:1
column3: Same as node_bin_shares:permissive:1. may_see_all_of never returns null.

column1: generate_inferred_history:guard:2
column3: Removing it looks up a template by a null variety, which matches nothing, so the next guard returns the same zero.

column1: generate_inferred_history:guard:3
column3: Removing it loops over the steps of a null template, which is no rows, so the count returned is the same zero.
